questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word: **JUVENILE**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Childish**.

• The word **"Juvenile"** refers to something related to young people, especially children or adolescents, or something immature. (नाबालिग/बालसुलभ)

 

 
• **Example:** The juvenile behavior of the students disrupted the class.

 

 

 
• **"Childish"** refers to behavior or actions that resemble those of a child and are often immature or silly. (बचकाना)

 

 
• **Example:** His childish argument showed a lack of seriousness.

 

 

 
• Hence, the word "Juvenile" closely relates to "Childish," making option 3 the correct answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Childish**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Adult** (वयस्क): Refers to a person who is fully grown or mature.

 

 
• **Example:** As an adult, he took full responsibility for his actions.

 

 

 
• **Wise** (बुद्धिमान): Having or showing experience, knowledge, and good judgment.

 

 
• **Example:** Her wise advice helped me solve the problem effectively.

 

 

 
• **Mature** (परिपक्व): Fully developed physically or mentally; showing maturity in behavior.

 

 
• **Example:** His mature response to the crisis impressed everyone.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. **Extirpate**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Establish**.

• **"Establish" **is the opposite of extirpate as it refers to creating or setting up something permanently or firmly. (स्थापित करना)
 
 
• **Example: **The company plans to establish a new office in the city.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the antonym of **"Extirpate"** is **"Establish"**.

• **Uproot **(जड़ से उखाड़ना): To pull out by the roots or completely remove something from its place.
 
 
• **Example: **The farmer uprooted the weeds from the field.
 
 
 
• **Eradicate** (समूल नष्ट करना): To destroy or eliminate completely.
 
 
• **Example:** Scientists are working to eradicate diseases from the world.

questions.question:
**Change the following from active to passive:**

The committee had been debating complex amendments when the bell rang.

options.text: Complex amendments had had been been debated by the committee when the bell rang.
Complex amendments had been being debated by the committee when the bell rang.
Complex amendments had be being debated by the committee when the bell rang.
Complex amendments had debated by the committee when the bell rang.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The committee had been debating complex amendments when the bell rang."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "complex amendments" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "had been debating" to "had been being debated" (past perfect continuous passive).
 
• Ensure the time clause "when the bell rang" remains at the end for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"Complex amendments had been being debated by the committee when the bell rang."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"Complex amendments had had been been debated by the committee when the bell rang." – Incorrect repetition of "had" and "been."
 
• **Option 3: **"Complex amendments had be being debated by the committee when the bell rang." – Incorrect verb form "had be being debated."
 
• **Option 4: **"Complex amendments had debated by the committee when the bell rang." – Incorrect structure, missing "been."
</ul

questions.question:
**Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word:**

The knight raised his __**pauldron**__ before mounting.

options.text: The blacksmith polished the steel pauldron until it gleamed.
The art historian admired the engraved pauldron of the effigy.
The biology student dissected the pauldron of the sea slug.
The museum displayed a 15th-century Italian pauldron.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"pauldron"** refers to a piece of armor used to protect the shoulder. (कंधे का कवच)

 
 
• **Example:** The knight raised his pauldron before going into battle.
 
 
 
• In Option 3, the word "pauldron" is used as a homonym because it refers to a part of the anatomy of a sea slug rather than a piece of armor. Here, it is a metaphorical or scientific use of the word. (समुद्री जीव के कंधे जैसा हिस्सा)
 
 
• **Example:** The biology student dissected the pauldron of the sea slug to study its anatomy.
 
 
 
• Homonyms are words that sound or are spelled the same but have different meanings. In this case, "pauldron" has two distinct meanings: a piece of armor and a part of a sea slug's anatomy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1:** The blacksmith polished the steel pauldron until it gleamed. (कवच को चमकाया)

 
 
• **Example:** The blacksmith ensured the knight's pauldron was in perfect condition before the tournament.
 

 
This refers to the literal armor piece and does not involve a homonym.

 
 
• **Option 2:** The art historian admired the engraved pauldron of the effigy. (प्रतिमा का अलंकृत कवच)
 
 
• **Example:** The effigy's pauldron was covered in intricate designs that reflected the era's craftsmanship.
 

 
This option also refers to the literal meaning of "pauldron" as a piece of armor.

 
 
• **Option 4:** The museum displayed a 15th-century Italian pauldron. (15वीं सदी का कवच)
 
 
• **Example:** The museum's pauldron was a rare artifact from the Renaissance period.
 

 
This statement refers to an actual historic artifact, not a homonym.

questions.question:
**A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.**

He said, "Do it right now."

options.text: He told to do it now.
He told me to do it at once.
He told me do it right now.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He told me to do it at once.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Command in Direct Speech:**
 
 
• The direct speech "Do it right now" is a command.
 
• In indirect speech, a command is usually reported using the verb "told" followed by the object (if specified) and the infinitive form of the verb (to + verb).
 
 
 
• **Time Phrase:**
 
 
• The phrase "right now" is replaced with "at once" in indirect speech, as it conveys the same urgency in reported speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• In indirect speech, quotation marks are removed.
 
• The sentence is rephrased to fit the structure of reported speech.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *He told me to do it at once.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** He said do it immediately.
 
 
• Incorrect format: "said" should be followed by "to" when reporting a command in indirect speech.
 
• Does not specify the object "me," making it incomplete.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** He told to do it now.
 
 
• Incomplete: Does not specify the object (e.g., "me").
 
• Incorrect time phrase: "now" should be converted to "at once" or "immediately" in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** He told me do it right now.
 
 
• Incorrect structure: Missing the infinitive "to" before the verb "do."
 
• The phrase "right now" should be converted to "at once" in indirect speech.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
**A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.**

The professor remarked that students needed to submit their papers before Friday.

options.text: "Students need to submit their papers before Friday," the professor remarked.
"Students needed to submit their papers before Friday," said the professor.
"Submit your papers before Friday," the professor instructed.
"You were to submit your papers before Friday," said the professor.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The professor remarked that students needed to submit their papers before Friday.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"students needed to submit" becomes "Students need to submit"**
 
 
• Indirect past tense "needed" is converted to the present tense "need" in direct speech to match the statement context.
 
 
 
• **"their papers" remains "their papers"**
 
 
• No pronoun changes are required, as the subject remains the same.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "remarked"
 
• Converted to: "the professor remarked," maintaining the tone of the statement.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "Students" and ends with a comma within the quotation marks.
 
• Reporting clause follows the quoted speech, starting with a lowercase letter after the comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"“Students need to submit their papers before Friday,” the professor remarked."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "Students needed to submit their papers before Friday," said the professor.
 
 
• The verb tense "needed" is incorrect for direct speech in this context.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Submit your papers before Friday," the professor instructed.
 
 
• The tone changes from a remark to an instruction, altering the meaning.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "You were to submit your papers before Friday," said the professor.
 
 
• The tense "were to submit" changes the meaning to a past obligation.
 
 
</ul

• The paragraph introduces machine learning and explains its functioning in a logical order.

• **Sentence 4 follows** as it describes how machine learning models are trained:

The algorithm improves its performance by analyzing vast amounts of input data and identifying underlying patterns. questions.question:
**Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph:**

1. The primary purpose of this process is to ensure that the food we eat is safe and does not contain harmful bacteria or other contaminants.

2. Food processing is a series of methods used to transform raw ingredients into consumable products.

3. These methods can range from simple actions like cutting and grinding to more complex procedures such as pasteurization and fermentation.

4. Furthermore, it also helps to preserve food, extend its shelf life, and enhance its nutritional value.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph begins with **Sentence 2**, which introduces the concept of food processing:
 
 
• "Food processing is a series of methods used to transform raw ingredients into consumable products."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 3** follows, as it describes the range of methods involved in food processing:
 
 
• "These methods can range from simple actions like cutting and grinding to more complex procedures such as pasteurization and fermentation."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 1** comes next, explaining the primary purpose of food processing:
 
 
• "The primary purpose of this process is to ensure that the food we eat is safe and does not contain harmful bacteria or other contaminants."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 4** concludes the paragraph, elaborating on the additional benefits of food processing:
 
 
• "Furthermore, it also helps to preserve food, extend its shelf life, and enhance its nutritional value."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **2, 3, 1, 4**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"Food processing is a series of methods used to transform raw ingredients into consumable products. These methods can range from simple actions like cutting and grinding to more complex procedures such as pasteurization and fermentation. The primary purpose of this process is to ensure that the food we eat is safe and does not contain harmful bacteria or other contaminants. Furthermore, it also helps to preserve food, extend its shelf life, and enhance its nutritional value."</div
